item.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Found Guilty in Deaths of 190 Children
item.description: A Kenyan cult leader who ordered adherents to fast until death in order to attain paradise has been convicted. The judicial ruling addresses the mass fatalities among minors linked to the group.

item.title: White House Establishes NIH Women's Health Office via Executive Order
item.description: US President Trump has signed a directive creating a dedicated women's health division within the National Institutes of Health. First Lady Melania Trump praised the executive step as a milestone for female healthcare in the United States.

item.title: Shashi Tharoor Rejects Regime Change Agenda, Emphasizes Free Polls
item.description: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor stated that India is distinct from Bangladesh and France, responding to remarks by BJP figures. He clarified that opposition groups are focused on securing transparent elections rather than overthrowing the administration.

item.title: Zelensky Aide Blames US Intelligence Limits for Ukrainian Casualties
item.description: Adviser Serhii Beskrestnov told the BBC that restrictions on US intelligence sharing leave insufficient time to warn citizens about incoming missile strikes. Meanwhile, the White House maintained that intelligence sharing policies remain unaltered.

item.title: Portuguese FA Disciplines Cristiano Ronaldo with Ban and Fine
item.description: The Portuguese Football Federation has penalized Cristiano Ronaldo with a 30-day ban and a £215 fine following his departure from the national team training camp during the previous month.

item.title: HRSS Reports 73 Deaths from Political Violence in Nine Months
item.description: Human rights group HRSS documented 73 political fatalities and 187 mob-related deaths over a nine-month period. According to the organization, 91 percent of political clashes stemmed from internal BNP disputes or conflicts between the BNP and other parties.

item.title: Independent MP Helen Haines Hospitalized After Vehicle Strike
item.description: Independent federal lawmaker Helen Haines is in critical condition at a Melbourne hospital after being hit by a vehicle in Wangaratta. A joint counter-terrorism unit is probing the collision, which Prime Minister Anthony Albanese suggested was intentional.

item.title: Unrest Prompts Curfews and Bans Across Several French Cities
item.description: Local authorities in Marseille prohibited public gatherings and demonstrations from noon until evening in response to ongoing civil unrest. Officials clarified that the measure constitutes targeted assembly restrictions rather than a formal curfew.

item.title: Florida middle schoolers turn classmate's wheelchair into angel costume
item.description: A group of 25 eighth-graders in Florida built an angel-themed throne around the wheelchair of nine-year-old Kaelyn Goodman. The project helped incorporate her mobility device into her requested princess angel Halloween outfit.

item.title: Amazon launches TorchNeuron tool to challenge Nvidia in AI chip market
item.description: Amazon introduced the TorchNeuron software development kit to encourage developers using the PyTorch AI framework to utilize its proprietary chips instead of Nvidia hardware.

item.title: Open-pit gold mine cave-in kills six individuals in southwestern Colombia
item.description: Official sources reported that six workers died on Monday following a cave-in at an open-pit gold mine located in a distant area of the Nariño department in Colombia.

item.title: England women's manager Sarina Wiegman faces new tasks after contract renewal
item.description: Following her significant impact on English women's soccer, national team coach Sarina Wiegman is preparing for new objectives after extending her contract.

item.title: Manchester United and Liverpool monitor Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha
item.description: Reports indicate that Premier League clubs Manchester United and Liverpool are tracking Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha as part of latest transfer rumors.

item.title: Finland pursues one million landmines amid concerns over Russian border
item.description: Finland has chosen to exit a United Nations treaty prohibiting landmines, aligning with neighboring nations as it prepares for potential security risks from Russia.

item.title: Afghanistan defeats Zimbabwe in cricket match with Atal and Rashid starring
item.description: Afghanistan secured a decisive victory after limiting Zimbabwe to 136 runs during a target chase of 295, denying their opponents a place in the final.

item.title: One person shot and killed near Columbus, Ohio mosque

item.title: Spanish military rescues stranded residents from roofs

item.title: Japan initiates first mission to study Martian moons

item.title: OpenCode AI programming tool breached by hackers
item.description: Malicious actors compromised the online platform of open-source coding assistant OpenCode, stealing user API keys and causing unexpected account charges. The compromised system attempted to seek assistance, but the linked AI tools declined to analyze the malicious code.
